reasons: No tests are visible in this file or packet.
Shape assumptions depend on a hand-copied type file that says to be kept in sync with the server.
Errors from the PDF and PowerPoint buttons are shown with alerts or messages, but tab views have no error boundary.

terms.meaning: a reusable piece of the screen, written as a function that returns what should be drawn
a value the screen remembers while it is open, such as the selected tab
a value passed into a component from the parent that uses it
a portable document file, here the one-page methodology note
a doorway other programs use to ask this app for data

sections.name: File setup, LL_DECK_API
sections.title: Imports and the deck API settings
sections.what: Brings in the pieces the results screen needs and defines `LL_DECK_API`, which tells the slide editor where to load and save this run's deck and what link to use back to the run.
sections.why: Keeps the slide editor reusable across tools. The link format is set here so the slide editor can point back to this run.
sections.watch_out: The run link format is hard-coded, so changing the page address means updating it here.

sections.name: TABS, ResultTab
sections.title: Tab list and tab type
sections.what: Lists the ten result tabs in order, with the label shown for each, and defines the type of a tab id.
sections.why: Keeps tab names and order in one place so the buttons and the type checks stay in step.
sections.watch_out: A new tab id must be added here and given a matching view in the render code, or it will show nothing.

sections.name: Panel, Kicker
sections.title: Panel and section heading styles
sections.what: Two small building blocks: a bordered white box that scrolls when its content is tall, and a small red uppercase label used above sections.
sections.why: Gives every view the same look without repeating the styling.

sections.name: Pill
sections.title: Tab button
sections.what: A single rounded button used for tabs and filters. It looks filled when selected and reports clicks to its parent.
sections.why: Shared by the tab bar, the outcome filter, the pillar selector and the evidence filters.

sections.name: RecipeResultView (part 1)
sections.title: Result screen state and methodology download
sections.what: Holds which tab is open, which evidence item is selected, and whether the case tab applies. It also starts the methodology PDF download and reports an error with an alert if it fails.
sections.why: Keeps the parts of the screen that depend on user choice in one place. Reason for using an alert for errors not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The selected tab can be controlled from outside (through the `tab` prop), so the internal tab state is ignored when that prop is set.

sections.name: RecipeResultView (part 2)
sections.title: Tab bar, export buttons and view switching
sections.what: Draws the tab bar, the PDF and PowerPoint buttons, the demo hints, and the chosen view. The slides tab can switch to a full slide editor that takes over the whole panel.
sections.why: This is the frame that every view sits inside. The editor takes over the slides tab so users can edit the deck directly.
sections.watch_out: The Recipes tab only shows when the run has cases, and the Yard coverage tab only shows when there is a run id.

sections.name: Overview (part 1)
sections.title: Overview headline and pillar bars
sections.what: Shows the scope name, the executive summary with citations, and one card per driver pillar. Each card has a colored bar showing strong, mixed and challenge evidence.
sections.why: Gives a quick read of the whole run before the user opens detailed tabs.
sections.watch_out: Pillar bars use the case grades when cases exist and fall back to the older assessment counts otherwise, so the two views can differ on older runs.

sections.name: Overview (part 2)
sections.title: Overview counts and source checks
sections.what: Shows the outcome counts (Delivered, Overran, and so on), a breakdown of how many sources were verified, unreachable or unsourced, and a note on facts held back for describing a different project.
sections.why: Lets the user judge how much of the evidence was checked before trusting the lessons.
sections.watch_out: The outcome chips fall back to a plain background color for unknown outcome names, so a new outcome label will show without its usual color.

sections.name: Pillars
sections.title: Pillar profile view
sections.what: Shows one pillar at a time: its principle, case stance counts, a written profile, practices that worked, implications, the scoring rubric, the sources it is grounded in, and its sub-drivers.
sections.why: Lets the user see the full reasoning behind one pillar.
sections.watch_out: The pillar selector starts on the first pillar, and if no pillars exist a message is shown instead.

sections.name: Drivers
sections.title: Sub-driver view
sections.what: Lists every sub-driver on the left and shows the chosen one on the right with its profile, good examples and cautionary tales. A gap message appears when no admitted fact supports the sub-driver.
sections.why: Shows the detail below each pillar, and makes gaps in the evidence visible rather than hidden.
sections.watch_out: Project names are looked up by id, so a project id missing from the project list will show a blank name.

sections.name: Cases
sections.title: Case list and case detail
sections.what: Shows the list of cited projects on the left, and on the right the chosen project's headline, outcome, takeaways, perspectives and admitted facts.
sections.why: Gives a per-project read of what went well and what went wrong.
sections.watch_out: The outcome text is shown as stored, so an outcome label that does not match the color map will appear without color.

sections.name: Matrix
sections.title: Heat map table
sections.what: Shows a table of projects against driver pillars, with each cell colored by score. Users can filter by outcome. Hovering over a cell shows the strength and challenge signal counts.
sections.why: Lets the user compare many projects against every pillar at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Only projects with at least one fact appear in the table, so a project with no facts will be silently left out.

sections.name: Evidence
sections.title: Evidence list and search
sections.what: Lists facts with filters for verification status and held-back facts, plus a search box that matches fact text or project name. Clicking a fact opens it in the evidence panel. Results load 150 at a time.
sections.why: Lets the user audit each fact and its source check.
sections.watch_out: Search and filters run on the whole fact list in the browser, so very large runs may feel slow. Reason for the 150 limit not stated in the code, but it keeps the page responsive.

sections.name: Method
sections.title: Method view
sections.what: Shows the research thesis, the methodology items with their quotes, the qualifications, the sources read with their capture status, the searches run, and the status of each search provider.
sections.why: Lets the user check how the method was built and whether the sources really support it.
sections.watch_out: Source links open in a new tab, and the page does not check whether those links still work.

sections.name: Slides
sections.title: Slide preview and navigation
sections.what: Shows a list of slide titles on the left and one slide at a time on the right, with previous and next buttons and a page counter.
sections.why: Lets the user preview the deck inside the app before exporting it.
sections.watch_out: The current slide number is kept in the view state, so if the deck changes while open the number may point to a different slide.

summary: The main results screen for a finished Lessons Learnt run, with ten tabs that show the same saved result in different views.
purpose: Lets a user read the lessons, project comparisons, evidence and method behind a recipe-v3 run, and export it as a PowerPoint or methodology PDF.
why: Likely reason: the result is one saved data set, so each tab is a different lens on it instead of a separate report. Reason for the split into separate tabs not stated in the code.
how: The top of `RecipeResultView` holds the selected tab and the selected evidence item. It shows tab buttons, export and PDF buttons, then renders one view component depending on the tab. The `Overview`, `Pillars`, `Drivers`, `Cases`, `Matrix`, `Evidence`, `Method` and `Slides` components each read one part of the result. Citation numbers come from `CiteProvider`. The evidence panel on the right opens when a citation or evidence row is clicked. In replay demos the slide editor is swapped for a read-only replay.
inputs: A `RecipeV3Result` object (the saved run result), an optional run id, export and tab-change callbacks, an optional replay deck and optional demo hints.
outputs: The rendered results workspace. It sends no data anywhere itself. Export and PDF downloads are started through callbacks and `downloadBlob`.
risks: Several tabs assume fields exist in the result, such as `r.totals.byOutcome` and `r.methodology.items`. Older runs without the `cases` section are handled by fallback views, but any missing field in a new result can cause a blank screen or error. The Evidence tab shows only the first 150 rows until the user clicks show more.
debug: If a tab is blank, check the browser console for an error naming a missing field, then compare the saved result against `types.ts`. If the Recipes tab is missing, the run has no cases. If Yard coverage is missing, the page has no run id. If export fails, look at the callback passed in from `RecipeRunView`.
